issues.title: Graphene, nickelates and a single copper–oxygen plane
issues.selectionBasis: Editorial selection across graphene, nickelates and cuprates, ordered by publication date. Not a popularity ranking or exhaustive literature feed.
issues.editorialNote: Initial selection preserved from 18 October 2026. This is the starting archive, not a record of earlier weekly editions. Original source-check dates have not been refreshed by this migration.

items.title: Probing broken time-reversal symmetry in graphene
items.paperTitle: Phase-sensitive signatures of time-reversal-symmetry-breaking superconductivity in magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene
items.summary: Josephson interferometry in magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene reveals asymmetric interference and field-sweep hysteresis below about 0.8 K, beneath the superconducting onset near 2 K.
items.limitation: The authors interpret these signatures as consistent with broken time-reversal symmetry; they do not uniquely establish a chiral pairing state.
items.verificationScope: Publisher abstract and publication-status notice; no full-text or independent replication review.
items.whyItMatters: Phase-sensitive probes help connect interference measurements to candidate superconducting symmetries.

items.title: Interlayer coherence in superconducting nickelates
items.paperTitle: Interlayer hybridization promotes superconductivity in bilayer nickelates
items.summary: X-ray spectroscopy of protected (La,Pr)3Ni2O7 films links superconductivity to coherent interlayer orbital hybridization, with oxygen content and epitaxial strain tuning the electronic states.
items.limitation: This film-specific evidence supports a multiorbital interpretation but does not by itself settle the pairing mechanism across nickelate families.
items.verificationScope: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record; subscription full text and raw data not reviewed.
items.whyItMatters: A material-specific link between orbital coherence and superconductivity guides comparisons between nickelate samples.

items.title: Superconductivity in a single copper–oxygen plane
items.paperTitle: Superconducting 2D cuprate with a single CuO2 plane
items.summary: Monolayer Bi-2201 retains superconductivity with one CuO2 plane, while controlled oxygenation reveals an intermediate anomalous metal and unusual scaling near the superconductor–insulator transition.
items.limitation: The reported phase behavior concerns this material and tuning protocol; its zero-temperature interpretation is inferred from finite-temperature measurements.
items.verificationScope: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record; subscription full text and raw data not reviewed.
items.whyItMatters: A single-plane platform helps isolate how dimensionality and oxygen tuning affect cuprate transport.
